heading: Four questions before buying life insurance for a child (73 seconds)
name: Life insurance for a child: four questions before you buy
description: Four questions for parents and grandparents before buying life insurance on a child: is the parents' own coverage in place, who owns and pays, can the child buy more coverage later, and what the cash value is and is not. General information, not advice.
transcript: Life insurance for a child: 4 questions before you buy. For parents and grandparents. Question 1. Are the parents covered? A child depends on your income. So parents should have their own coverage in place first. Question 2. Who owns the policy, and who pays? A parent or grandparent buys it. Premiums are paid for many years. Ask how ownership transfers when the child is an adult. Question 3. Can the child buy more coverage later? Many policies include the right to buy more at set ages, without health questions. Ask if the policy includes it, and what it costs. Question 4. What is the cash value, and what is it not? It builds slowly, and it is small in the early years. The owner can borrow against it. It is not a college savings plan or a savings account. Saving for education? Compare dedicated options too. We do not say life insurance is better or worse than a 529 plan. Each has different purposes, costs and tax treatment. Want to talk it through? Schedule a time at honorbrook-insurance.com or call (301) 615-8289.
